184 - Private health insurance If your employer pays all or part of your private health insurance premiums, you may be entitled to claim a deduction for the amount they pay. However, you cannot claim a deduction if your total income plus Medicare levy exceeds a certain limit (see below). If you are self-employed, you can claim a deduction for any private health insurance premiums that you pay. You can also claim a deduction for any private health insurance policies you take out to cover the income of your associates. Deductions are not available for the cost of hospitalisation, treatment or other services even though these costs are often covered by private health insurance. Private Health Insurance Deductions Limits The following limits apply to how much you can claim in deductions for private health insurance. If you are not eligible for the government rebate on private health insurance. Instead, you can claim a deduction for the amount your spouse's policy actually costs. How to claim a deduction When completing your tax return, print out the private health insurance statement from the Medicare website and enter the amounts shown in the ATO online portal. Alternatively, you can contact your health fund directly for a copy of your private health insurance statement.
